judge.rationale: The candidate preserves all factual content and the scheduling intent from the Russian: it declines Saturday evening and proposes Sunday afternoon, conditional on the other person's availability. Phrasing choices like “sábado de noche” and “después del mediodía” are understandable but a bit less idiomatic than local alternatives (e.g. “el sábado por la noche” or “el sábado a la noche”, and “el domingo por la tarde” or “después del almuerzo”), which is why naturalness is not rated perfect. No facts were added or omitted.

cases.recommended_reply: Ya escribí tres veces por la canilla que pierde en la cocina y hasta ahora nadie vino. De verdad necesito ayuda hoy o, por lo menos, mañana de mañana.
cases.source_text: Я уже три раза писал про протекающий кран на кухне, и до сих пор никто не пришёл. Мне правда нужна помощь сегодня или хотя бы завтра утром.

judge.rationale: The candidate preserves the original meaning and urgency: the speaker has written three times about a leaking kitchen faucet and still no one has come, and they need help today or at least tomorrow morning. Small issues affect naturalness: “hasta ahora nadie vino” uses simple past instead of the more natural present perfect (e.g. “no ha venido”), but is understandable. “Por la canilla que pierde” is acceptable in Rioplatense Spanish (canilla is fine), though "que gotea" or "que está goteando" would sound more natural. The main problem is “mañana de mañana,” which is ungrammatical/unnatural for “tomorrow morning” (expected: “mañana por la mañana” or “mañana temprano”). No facts were added or omitted. Overall understandable for an A2 user but needs small phrasing fixes to sound natural in es-UY.
